grammar.title: Extremely with 形容词 + 极了
grammar.explanation: 极了 (jíle) goes right after an adjective to mean "extremely, to the max" — a stronger, more colloquial version of 很 or 非常. It always comes after the adjective, never before, and often ends the sentence.

grammar.title: The more... the more... with 越...越...
grammar.explanation: 越...越... (yuè...yuè...) links two changes that happen together — "the more A, the more B". Both clauses use 越 before a verb or adjective, showing they rise or fall in step.

sentences.zh: 虽然很难，我们也要坚持下去。
sentences.pinyin: Suīrán hěn nán, wǒmen yě yào jiānchí xiàqù.
sentences.en: Even though it's hard, we still have to keep persisting.
He decided to keep doing it.
He kept writing on and on.

sentences.zh: 他学习很努力，并且成绩很好。
sentences.pinyin: Tā xuéxí hěn nǔlì, bìngqiě chéngjì hěn hǎo.
sentences.en: He studies very hard, and moreover his grades are good.

sentences.zh: 公司决定开始这个计划，并且马上行动。
sentences.pinyin: Gōngsī juédìng kāishǐ zhège jìhuà, bìngqiě mǎshàng xíngdòng.
sentences.en: The company decided to start this plan, and take action right away.

sentences.zh: 我们讨论了这个问题，并且找到了办法。
sentences.pinyin: Wǒmen tǎolùn le zhège wèntí, bìngqiě zhǎodào le bànfǎ.
sentences.en: We discussed this problem and found a solution.
He caught hold of the ball.
